content.content:
1	Equipment is frequently attached to the outside of a pipe after the pipe has been installed. Sensors, small tools, brackets, and lengths of conduit all have to be carried on a pipe that cannot be taken out of service, cannot be lifted, and has no free end over which a closed ring could be threaded. A clamp intended for that duty therefore has to open from the side, close around the pipe, and grip it firmly enough that the carried equipment keeps its position, while remaining removable so that the same clamp can be taken off and used again elsewhere.
2	
3	A clamp that opens from the side is split into parts, and the split is what makes the gripping problem difficult. Once the clamp body is divided, any drive element that runs around the body is divided with it. Gripping arrangements that answer this by driving the gripping surfaces of each part separately give up the fixed relationship between the two parts of the drive: the two sides of the clamp advance by amounts that depend on how each side is operated, so the clamp tends to settle off center on the pipe, and the load is shared unevenly between the gripping surfaces. Arrangements that instead pull the split body closed on the pipe, in the manner of a band or a two-bolt saddle, transfer the closing force through the joint at the split and rely on the pipe itself to react the closing motion, so the grip depends on how nearly the bore of the clamp matches the outside diameter of the pipe. Such an arrangement is commonly supplied with liners or inserts machined for one nominal pipe size, and a different pipe size calls for a different insert or a different clamp.
4	
5	Reusable clamping also has to deal with the force the operator applies. A hand lever gives the operator no measure of what has been done to the pipe. When the gripping elements have reached the pipe, further travel of the lever has to go somewhere, and in a rigid drive train it goes into whichever gripping element happens to touch first, so that one gripping surface is loaded far more than the others. Thin walled tube, coated pipe, and lined pipe are all damaged by that kind of concentrated loading, and the operator has no indication that it has occurred. Torque tools and gauges can be added to the installation, but they add a separate instrument to the task and, when they respond to the position of the gripping elements, they report the size of the pipe rather than the force in the grip.
6	
7	What has been lacking is a split clamp in which the drive that advances the gripping elements is itself restored to a single, continuous element by the act of closing the clamp, in which every gripping element is advanced from that one drive so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes, and in which the travel remaining in the operator's lever after the gripping elements have landed on the pipe is absorbed within the clamp and reported to the operator as a loading condition rather than as a dimension.
8

1	The following description of embodiments refers to the accompanying drawings. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout. Terms of direction are used with respect to the frame of the clamp: the axis of the frame is the axis about which the frame is annular in the closed condition, "inward" and "radially inward" mean toward that axis, "outward" and "radially outward" mean away from it, and "circumferential" means about that axis. These terms describe relationships within the clamp and do not require the clamp to be used in any particular attitude.
2	
3	Overall arrangement
4	
5	FIG. 1 shows a split pipe clamp 100 in the closed condition around a pipe 90. The clamp 100 has a first frame half 10 and a second frame half 12. Each of the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 is semicircular, and the two frame halves together surround the pipe 90. The first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are joined at one end, referred to as the hinge end, by a hinge 14, and are releasably joined at the other end, referred to as the latch end, by a releasable latch 16. The hinge 14 permits the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 to be swung apart far enough for the clamp 100 to be passed sideways onto a pipe 90 that is already installed, so that the clamp 100 need not be threaded over a free end of the pipe 90. When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame that is annular about the axis of the clamp 100.
6	
7	Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.
8	
9	The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring 20 nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
10	
11	The segmented cam ring
12	
13	FIG. 2 shows the segmented cam ring 20 of the clamp 100, drawn removed from the frame with its segments in the coupled condition. The segmented cam ring 20 comprises a first cam ring segment 22 and a second cam ring segment 24. ## Ledger result (abridged)

The overwhelming majority of the draft traces cleanly to the disclosure: split frame halves + hinge + releasable latch, semicircular halves, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads, no diameter-specific tooling, segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per half, complementary drive faces at both ends coupling on closure, followers in oblique slots, wedge driven by the latch against a ring drive face, limited stroke, synchronized inward travel, outward carriage springs, two latch positions with the second over-center, force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range, "reports loading, not diameter," the install/remove sequence, and the optional non-participating mounting boss. Numerals are one-to-one, all 25 are used, and no drafting notes, placeholders, or open questions remain in `draft/` or `figures/`. Figure geometry is internally consistent (I verified the FIG. 2 slot handedness against FIG. 4's mirrored view and the clockwise drive sense — it checks out).

Six issues fall short of full traceability or clarity; none is critical.

input.summary: Full source-ledger trace of the p9 draft (title through abstract, numeral table, and FIG-1 through FIG-5 briefs) against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md. The core mechanism is fully supported: split semicircular frame halves with hinge and releasable latch; three radial jaw carriages in radial guides with pivoting concave jaw pads and no diameter-specific insert; a segmented cam ring in an annular guide, one segment per half, coupled at hinge and latch ends by complementary drive faces on closure; followers in oblique slots converting a limited ring stroke into synchronized inward jaw travel; a wedge driven by the latch against a ring drive face; carriage return springs; first (holding) and second (over-center) latch positions; a force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge absorbing remaining travel; an indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range and reporting load rather than diameter; the install/remove sequence; and the optional non-participating mounting boss. Numerals are one-to-one and all 25 are used; no drafting notes, placeholders, or unresolved alternatives remain; figure geometry is internally consistent, including the FIG. 2 slot handedness checked against FIG. 4's expressly mirrored view and clockwise drive sense; the abstract is 145 words; cross-reference and government-support sections match the brief (no priority claim, no federal sponsorship). Six findings remain: one major untraced set of latch-housing structural relationships, and five minor items covering a spring reaction member, two prior-art-derived negative limitations, an undescribed drive-train element in the FIG. 4 brief, and an unstated viewing side in the FIG. 2 brief. Note that the prior-art set in prior_art/ was not searched and may be incomplete; Background prior-art characterizations were not traced here and are left to the later citation review.

findings.title: Latch housing structural relationships (mounted on frame, handle pivoted to housing, wedge inside housing) are untraced
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "FIG. 4 shows the latch 16 in fragmentary section" (line 37)
findings.detail: The description assigns three concrete structural relationships to the latch housing that no inventor passage states. The disclosure mentions the latch housing exactly once, and only as the carrier of a reference edge for the indicator pin: "A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range." It never says the housing is mounted on the frame, never says the latch handle is pivotally mounted on the housing, and never says the wedge is guided inside the housing. There is a second defect in the same clause: paragraph 5 defines the frame as coming into existence only on closure ("When the frame halves are brought together and the latch 16 is engaged, the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 define a frame"), so a housing "mounted on the frame" has no host in the open condition, and a latch that releasably joins the two halves must in fact be carried by one half and engage the other. The FIG. 4 brief already quarantines this geometry as convention ("Shown schematically: ... the latch housing and its cavity, the gap through which the latch handle 50 passes, the linkage by which it acts on the flat plate"), so the figure needs no change; only the description text asserts the relationships.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 mounted on the frame at the latch end, a latch handle 50 pivotally mounted on the latch housing 58, a wedge 52 movable in the latch housing 58, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52." Nearest source (no affirmative passage exists for the mounting, the pivot, or the wedge guidance): "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge" and "A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing" (disclosure.md line 9).
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 at the latch end, a latch handle 50, a wedge 52, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The latch housing 58 presents a fixed edge referred to below in connection with the indicator pin 56." Make no other change; the FIG. 4 brief already labels the housing, cavity, gap and linkage as shown schematically.

findings.title: Carriage return spring's reaction member and seating location are not disclosed
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame" (line 33); figures/FIG-3.md line 15
findings.detail: The disclosure states only the biasing function, not what the spring reacts against or where it sits. The description fixes the reaction member as the frame, and the FIG. 3 brief further places the spring inside the radial guide channel acting on the channel wall. The reaction against the frame is close to inherent (the frame is the only body guiding the carriage), and the FIG. 3 brief does mark the spring and its seats as schematic, so this is minor; but the description text asserts a connection the inventor never described.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward." Candidate (FIG-3.md): "A compression spring is drawn as a zigzag line acting between the jaw carriage 30 and the wall of the channel so as to urge the jaw carriage 30 upward, that is, radially outward". Nearest source: "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released." (disclosure.md line 7). No affirmative passage identifies a reaction member or seat.
findings.fix: In the description, change to: "A carriage return spring 44 acts on each jaw carriage 30 so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward." Leave the FIG. 3 brief as drawn, since it already states "The carriage return spring and its seats are shown schematically."

findings.title: Negative limitation "without an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter" traces only to the Background's prior-art characterization
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claim 5; draft/06-summary.md line 5; draft/08-detailed-description.md lines 7 and 31
findings.detail: "Insert" is a prior-art term introduced in the Background ("commonly supplied with liners or inserts machined for one nominal pipe size"). The inventor never uses it. A negative structural limitation in a claim needs its own affirmative support; the inventor's statement is a functional one about the jaw pad, not a statement that no insert component is present. The substance (grips a range of diameters, no size-specific tooling) is fully supported and should be kept; only the borrowed component noun should go.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 5): "whereby the split pipe clamp grips pipes of different diameters within a radial travel of the jaw carriages without an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter." Nearest source: "Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter." (disclosure.md line 5). The word "insert" appears nowhere in disclosure.md or in the USER passage of conversation.md.
findings.fix: In claim 5, summary line 5, and description lines 7 and 31, replace "without an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter" (and "no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required") with "without a part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter" (and "no part dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required"). Leave the Background wording unchanged.

findings.title: Mounting boss recited as "connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any jaw carriage" where the inventor stated only a functional non-participation
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md claims 8 and 10; draft/06-summary.md line 9; draft/08-detailed-description.md line 9
findings.detail: The claims convert the inventor's functional statement into a structural negative limitation about connections. The two are not equivalent: a boss could be connected to the frame's ring channel and still not participate in synchronization. Because this is a narrowing limitation in claims 8 and 10, it needs support in its own terms. The supported form is available verbatim from the disclosure and is at least as narrow in effect.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 8): "further comprising a mounting boss on the frame outside the annular guide and arranged to support a sensor, a tool, or a conduit, the mounting boss being connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any of the jaw carriages." Nearest source: "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization." (disclosure.md line 13).
findings.fix: In claims 8 and 10, replace "the mounting boss being connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any of the jaw carriages" with "the mounting boss not participating in the synchronized advance of the jaw carriages". Make the parallel substitution in summary line 9 and in the description sentence at line 9, which may then read: "The mounting boss 70 does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30."

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief introduces an unnumbered flat plate in the latch drive train that appears nowhere in the description
findings.detail: The disclosed drive train is handle -> force-limiting spring stack -> wedge. The figure brief inserts a further element, a flat plate across the cavity that seats the spring stack and is pressed by an arm from the handle pivot. The plate is not numbered, not described in draft/08-detailed-description.md, and has no inventor support. The brief does mark it schematic, but the depiction can be simplified so the figure shows only the disclosed force path, which removes the mismatch between the figure and the description without adding anything to the application text.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Above it, the force-limiting spring stack 54 is a zigzag spring line from the wedge 52 to a flat plate across the cavity." and "A short schematic arm reaches from that pivot down and to the left and presses down on the flat plate." Nearest source: "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge" (disclosure.md line 9). No affirmative passage describes a plate, seat, or intermediate linkage member.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, delete the flat plate: change line 11 to "Above it, the force-limiting spring stack 54 is a zigzag spring line rising from the wedge 52 into the upper part of the cavity."; change the arm sentence to "A short schematic arm reaches from that pivot down and to the left and presses down on the upper end of the force-limiting spring stack 54."; and delete "the flat plate spring seat," and "the linkage by which it acts on the flat plate," from the schematic list in line 3, replacing the latter with "the linkage by which it acts on the force-limiting spring stack 54". Add nothing to the description or claims.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief asserts a rotation sense shared with FIG. 4 without stating which side the ring is viewed from
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md lines 3 and 13; draft/07-drawings.md FIG. 2 entry
findings.detail: FIG. 4 expressly declares a mirrored viewpoint ("viewed from the side of that plane opposite to the side from which FIG. 1 is viewed"), so any cross-figure statement about clockwise versus counterclockwise depends on the viewing side. FIG. 2 states a slot handedness and ties it to the drive sense in FIG. 4, but never says which side of the ring it is viewed from. The intended reading is the same side as FIG. 1, and under that reading the two briefs are consistent (wedge drives segment 24 away from the latch joint, which is clockwise in the FIG. 1 orientation, and each slot's inner end lying counterclockwise of its outer end then produces inward follower travel). The ambiguity should be closed in the brief so the renderer cannot mirror FIG. 2 and invert the mechanism.
findings.evidence: Candidate (FIG-2.md line 13): "In each slot the end nearer the inner boundary lies counterclockwise of the end nearer the outer boundary, as viewed here, so that clockwise rotation of the ring, the sense in which the wedge drives it in FIG. 4, brings the inner portion of each slot to the circumferential position held by its outer portion." FIG-2.md line 3 states only "viewed along the axis of the ring", with no side declared, while FIG-4.md line 3 declares "viewed along the axis of the frame from the side opposite that of FIG. 1".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md line 3, change "viewed along the axis of the ring" to "viewed along the axis of the ring from the same side as FIG. 1 is viewed, so that the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right". No change to draft/07-drawings.md or to the description is required.

findings.detail: The claims convert the inventor's functional statement into a structural negative limitation about connections. The two are not equivalent: a boss could be connected to the frame's ring channel and still not participate in synchronization. Because this is a narrowing limitation in claims 8 and 10, it needs support in its own terms. The supported form is available verbatim from the disclosure and is at least as narrow in effect.
findings.evidence: Candidate (claim 8): "further comprising a mounting boss on the frame outside the annular guide and arranged to support a sensor, a tool, or a conduit, the mounting boss being connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any of the jaw carriages." Nearest source: "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization." (disclosure.md line 13).
findings.fix: In claims 8 and 10, replace "the mounting boss being connected neither to the segmented cam ring nor to any of the jaw carriages" with "the mounting boss not participating in the synchronized advance of the jaw carriages". Make the parallel substitution in summary line 9 and in the description sentence at line 9, which may then read: "The mounting boss 70 does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30."

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief introduces an unnumbered flat plate in the latch drive train that appears nowhere in the description
findings.detail: The disclosed drive train is handle -> force-limiting spring stack -> wedge. The figure brief inserts a further element, a flat plate across the cavity that seats the spring stack and is pressed by an arm from the handle pivot. The plate is not numbered, not described in draft/08-detailed-description.md, and has no inventor support. The brief does mark it schematic, but the depiction can be simplified so the figure shows only the disclosed force path, which removes the mismatch between the figure and the description without adding anything to the application text.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Above it, the force-limiting spring stack 54 is a zigzag spring line from the wedge 52 to a flat plate across the cavity." and "A short schematic arm reaches from that pivot down and to the left and presses down on the flat plate." Nearest source: "A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge" (disclosure.md line 9). No affirmative passage describes a plate, seat, or intermediate linkage member.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, delete the flat plate: change line 11 to "Above it, the force-limiting spring stack 54 is a zigzag spring line rising from the wedge 52 into the upper part of the cavity."; change the arm sentence to "A short schematic arm reaches from that pivot down and to the left and presses down on the upper end of the force-limiting spring stack 54."; and delete "the flat plate spring seat," and "the linkage by which it acts on the flat plate," from the schematic list in line 3, replacing the latter with "the linkage by which it acts on the force-limiting spring stack 54". Add nothing to the description or claims.

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief asserts a rotation sense shared with FIG. 4 without stating which side the ring is viewed from
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md lines 3 and 13; draft/07-drawings.md FIG. 2 entry
findings.detail: FIG. 4 expressly declares a mirrored viewpoint ("viewed from the side of that plane opposite to the side from which FIG. 1 is viewed"), so any cross-figure statement about clockwise versus counterclockwise depends on the viewing side. FIG. 2 states a slot handedness and ties it to the drive sense in FIG. 4, but never says which side of the ring it is viewed from. The intended reading is the same side as FIG. 1, and under that reading the two briefs are consistent (wedge drives segment 24 away from the latch joint, which is clockwise in the FIG. 1 orientation, and each slot's inner end lying counterclockwise of its outer end then produces inward follower travel). The ambiguity should be closed in the brief so the renderer cannot mirror FIG. 2 and invert the mechanism.
findings.evidence: Candidate (FIG-2.md line 13): "In each slot the end nearer the inner boundary lies counterclockwise of the end nearer the outer boundary, as viewed here, so that clockwise rotation of the ring, the sense in which the wedge drives it in FIG. 4, brings the inner portion of each slot to the circumferential position held by its outer portion." FIG-2.md line 3 states only "viewed along the axis of the ring", with no side declared, while FIG-4.md line 3 declares "viewed along the axis of the frame from the side opposite that of FIG. 1".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md line 3, change "viewed along the axis of the ring" to "viewed along the axis of the ring from the same side as FIG. 1 is viewed, so that the hinge end is at the left and the latch end at the right". No change to draft/07-drawings.md or to the description is required.
